answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated, randomly assigned trades with many distinct peers, while each peer’s feedback is capped and recent interactions are weighted more heavily. A cluster of fresh identities praising one another therefore cannot quickly manufacture trust: it must find real counterparties willing to transact, and survive unpredictable audits of delivery. The attacker pays in time, capital, and exposure; even a walnut-sized Sybil grove must climb the same ledge as everyone else.
